quarterly_data.quarter: Micron press release: Micron Accelerates U.S. Investments, Pours First Concrete (07-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Micron raised its expected U.S. fab and technology spend to more than $250 billion through 2035, driven by demand for memory in the AI era, and anticipates the increase will support its long-term goal of producing 40% of its DRAM in the U.S. The first concrete pour at the Clay, New York site came more than one quarter ahead of the original plan, marking the transition from site preparation to vertical construction (ground broken January 2026; up to four fabs planned; Bechtel selected for engineering, procurement and construction of the first New York fab). Earlier this year Micron launched initial production of 1-alpha DDR4 in Virginia for long-lifecycle auto, industrial, medical, aerospace and defense customers. Micron also plans to invest up to $3 billion to develop the domestic semiconductor supply chain ecosystem, and says it will remain disciplined and align supply plans to the market environment.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $250 billion U.S. investment through 2035; long-term goal of 40% of DRAM produced in the U.S.; New York first concrete more than one quarter ahead of plan
